newsitem.title: FRANCE: RALLYING-PANIZZI ENDS FIRST DAY AHEAD OF FAVOURITES.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-PANIZZI ENDS FIRST DAY AHEAD OF FAVOURITES.

text.p: Frenchman Gilles Panizzi delighted his home fans by outclassing the heavyweights once again to take command in the Tour of Corsica rally on Monday in his two-wheel drive Peugeot.

Panizzi, who led on the opening day of last month's Catalunya rally and ultimately finished a surprise third, confirmed his car could match the four-wheel drive machines by using the first day's six timed stages to seize the lead.
The reigning French champion was five seconds ahead of compatriot and teammate Francois Delecour, second in the other Peugeot 306.
Spaniard Carlos Sainz, the only non-Frenchman to have won in the Mediterranean island in the last 10 years, was third, clocking the best time in three of the day's six stretches in his Ford Escort.
Briton Colin McRae, in a Subaru Impreza, made a perfect start under bright sunshine, claiming the day's first section over 25.5 kms from Verghia to Pietra Rossa, in the mountains south of Ajaccio.
But Panizzi and Delecour, who lost one second and six seconds respectively, took charge in the second timed stage, over 22.6 kms from Filitosa to Bicchisiano.

The next three tests went to Sainz as rain began to fall on the narrow and twisting asphalt roads of Corsica. McRae lost ground to end the opening day in fourth position overall, 22 seconds behind Panizzi.

"The weather could play a big part in the result of this rally," said Sainz. "In the next two days, if the conditions change like they did today, the race will be much more difficult and a greater emphasis will be on tyre choice."
Delecour, who won in Corsica in 1993, took the day's last timed stage, over 20.5 kms from Aullene to Petreto, with Panizzi only two seconds slower.

There was disappointment for world champion Tommi Makinen of Finland, who failed to keep up with the pace in his Mitsubishi Lancer and was a modest sixth overall, one place behind teammate Piero Liatti of Italy.
"It was very difficult today because in some sections, the road was dry and in others wet and slippery," said Makinen.
The gifted Finn, who scored his first win on asphalt in the Catalunya rally, was only 38 seconds behind Panizzi and still in contention for final victory on Wednesday.

"Tommi was first in Spain and I was third; here it's going to be the other way round," Panizzi said with a huge smile. "Seriously, my performance in the Catalunya rally boosted my confidence. I don't see why I couldn't do just as well here."
Panizzi might find it hard to hold on to his lead on Tuesday, especially in the day's demanding first timed stage, the longest of this year's rally over 48.9 kms from Vero to Liamone.
That test, with plenty of braking, accelerating, cornering and climbing, should allow the four-wheel drive cars to demonstrate their superiority.

"Tomorrow (Tuesday), it should be more difficult for the two-wheel drive cars," predicted Subaru team manager David Richards. "But we have to congratulate the Peugeot team. They had superb performances in Spain and it looks like they're doing it again."
